3	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4	related:
5	  links:
6	    - app/getting-started/caching

10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
59	
60	## Version History
61	
62	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
63	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
65

It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async. 18 19 > **Good to know:** 20 > 21 > - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern. 22 > - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees. 23 > - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 24 25 ## Usage 26 27 `use cache` is a Cache Components feature. Cached functions and components must be async: 49 50 ```tsx 51 // Function level 52 export async function getData() { 53 'use cache' 54 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 55 const data = await res.json() 56 return data 57 } 58 59 // Component level 60 export async function MyComponent() { 61 'use cache' 62 return <> 63 } 64 ``` 65 66 When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async: 67 68 ```tsx 69 // File level 70 'use cache' 71 72 export default async function Page() { 73 // ... 74 } 75 ``` 76 77 ## How `use cache` works 78 79 ### Cache keys 80 81 A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes: 82 83 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes. 84 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase 85 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments 86 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement 87 88 When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key. 89 90 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 91 async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) { 92 const getData = async (filter: string) => { 93 'use cache' 94 // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument) 95 const res = await fetch( 96 `https://api.example.com/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}` 97 ) 98 return res.json() 99 } 100 101 return getData('active') 102 } 103 ``` 104 105 In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries. 106 107 > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key. 108 109 ### Cache output 110 111 A cached function produces the same output for the same inputs. The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts. 112 113 Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation). 114 115 ```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts" 116 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 117 118 export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) { 119 'use cache' 120 cacheLife('hours') 121 122 const orders = await getOrders(accountId) 123 const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId) 124 125 return { orders, totals } 126 } 127 128 export async function getOrders(accountId: string) { 129 'use cache' 130 cacheLife('hours') 131 132 return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } }) 133 } 134 135 export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) { 136 return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } }) 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. Calls to `getOrders` have their own entries, keyed by the same `accountId`. If an earlier call, through the summary or directly, already filled one, `db.orders.findMany` doesn't run and those orders become part of the summary's output. See [nested caching behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-caching-behavior) for how an inner lifetime affects the entry around it. 141 142 Note that `getOrderTotals` is not cached. It is exported so other parts of the application can read fresh totals in an uncached scope. Inside `getOrderSummary`, though, the totals query only runs when that function runs following the `'hours'` lifetime set there. 143 144 With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prerendering fills the entry and keeps rendering, so this output contributes to the route's [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) and can contribute to its [prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prefetching). A cache life too short to store safely leaves a hole that resolves at request time instead. See [prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for the thresholds. 145 146 ## Serialization 147 148 Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable. 149 150 For a complete reference, see: 151 152 - [Serializable arguments](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) - Uses **React Server Components** serialization 153 - [Serializable return types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types) - Uses **React Client Components** serialization 154 155 > **Good to know:** Arguments and return values use different serialization systems. Server Component serialization (for arguments) is more restrictive than Client Component serialization (for return values). This means you can return JSX elements but cannot accept them as arguments unless using pass-through patterns. 156 157 ### Supported types 158 159 **Arguments:** 160 161 - Primitives: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined` 162 - Plain objects: `{ key: value }` 163 - Arrays: `[1, 2, 3]` 164 - Dates, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, ArrayBuffers 165 - React elements (as pass-through only) 166 167 **Return values:** 168 169 - Same as arguments, plus JSX elements 170 171 ### Unsupported types 172 173 - Class instances 174 - Functions (except as pass-through) 175 - Symbols, WeakMaps, WeakSets 176 - URL instances 177 178 ```tsx filename="app/components/user-card.tsx" 179 // Valid - primitives and plain objects 180 async function UserCard({ 181 id, 182 config, 183 }: { 184 id: string 185 config: { theme: string } 186 }) { 187 'use cache' 188 return
{id}
189 } 190 191 // Invalid - class instance 192 async function UserProfile({ user }: { user: UserClass }) { 193 'use cache' 194 // Error: Cannot serialize class instance 195 return
{user.name}
196 } 197 ``` 198 199 ### Pass-through (non-serializable arguments) 200 201 You can accept non-serializable values **as long as you don't introspect them**. This enables composition patterns with `children` and Server Actions: 202 203 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-wrapper.tsx" 204 async function CachedWrapper({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { 205 'use cache' 206 // Don't read or modify children - just pass it through 207 return ( 208
209
Cached Header
210 {children} 211
212 ) 213 } 214 215 // Usage: children can be dynamic 216 export default function Page() { 217 return ( 218 219 {/* Not cached, passed through */} 220 221 ) 222 } 223 ``` 224 225 You can also pass Server Actions through cached components: 226 227 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-form.tsx" 228 async function CachedForm({ action }: { action: () => Promise }) { 229 'use cache' 230 // Don't call action here - just pass it through 231 return
{/* ... */}
232 } 233 ``` 234 235 ## Constraints 236 237 Cached functions execute in an isolated environment. The following constraints ensure cache behavior remains predictable and secure. 238 239 ### Request-time APIs 240 241 Cached functions and components **cannot** access runtime APIs like `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, and the restriction follows the call stack: a helper the cached function calls that reads one of these fails the same way, with the [`next-request-in-use-cache`](/docs/messages/next-request-in-use-cache) error. On a dynamically rendered route this surfaces when the route runs, so it can pass `next build` and fail under `next start`. Read these values outside the cached scope and pass them as arguments. 242 243 ### Runtime caching considerations 244 245 While `use cache` is designed primarily to include uncached data in the static shell, it can also cache data at runtime using in-memory LRU (Least Recently Used) storage. 246 247 With the default in-memory handler, runtime cache behavior depends on your hosting environment: 248 249 | Environment | Runtime Caching Behavior | 250 | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 251 | **Serverless** | Cache entries typically don't persist across requests (each request can be a different instance), or during revalidation. Build-time caching works normally. | 252 | **Self-hosted** | Cache entries persist across requests. Control cache size with [`cacheMaxMemorySize`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheMaxMemorySize). | 253 254 For example, in a serverless environment, a cached function shared by two pages executes on each static shell revalidation, whereas in self-hosted or environments with persistent memory, the cached output is reused if it's still fresh. 255 256 If the default in-memory cache isn't enough, consider **[`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote)** which allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler (like Redis or KV database). This helps reduce hits against data sources not scaled to your total traffic, though it comes with costs (storage, network latency, platform fees). 257 258 > [!NOTE] 259 > With the default in-memory handler, serverless instances are ephemeral, so entries may not be reused between requests, unlike with `use cache: remote`. Neither caching directive carries over to a new deploy, because the [cache key](#cache-keys) includes the build (or `deploymentId`) ID. 260 > 261 > For data that needs to persist across deploys, use [`unstable_cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) for non-`fetch` functions or the [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) cache. 262 263 Very rarely, for compliance requirements or when you can't refactor your code to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, you might need [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 264 265 ### Draft Mode 266 267 When [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) is enabled, all cached functions and components re-execute on every request, and results are not saved to the cache. This ensures draft content is always fresh without requiring any changes to your caching code. 268 269 You can read `isEnabled` from [`draftMode()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) inside a `use cache` scope, however, other runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()` are not allowed, even when Draft Mode is active. See [Passing runtime values to cached functions](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#passing-runtime-values-to-cached-functions) for the recommended pattern. 270 271 ```tsx filename="app/components/content.tsx" 272 import { draftMode } from 'next/headers' 273 274 async function Content() { 275 'use cache' 276 277 const { isEnabled } = await draftMode() 278 const url = isEnabled 279 ? 'https://draft.example.com/content' 280 : 'https://production.example.com/content' 281 282 const data = await fetch(url) 283 return
{/* ... */}
284 } 285 ``` 286 287 Calling `enable()` or `disable()` inside a caching directive scope will also throw an error. Draft Mode can only be toggled in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). 288 289 ### React.cache isolation 290 291 [`React.cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) operates in an isolated scope inside `use cache` boundaries. Values stored via `React.cache` outside a `use cache` function are not visible inside it. 292 293 This means you cannot use `React.cache` to pass data into a `use cache` scope: 294 295 ```tsx 296 import { cache } from 'react' 297 298 const store = cache(() => ({ current: null as string | null })) 299 300 function Parent() { 301 const shared = store() 302 shared.current = 'value from parent' 303 return 304 } 305 306 async function Child() { 307 'use cache' 308 const shared = store() 309 // shared.current is null, not 'value from parent' 310 // use cache has its own isolated React.cache scope 311 return
{shared.current}
312 } 313 ``` 314 315 This isolation ensures cached functions have predictable, self-contained behavior. To pass data into a `use cache` scope, use function arguments instead. 316 317 ## `use cache` at runtime 318 319 On the **server**, cache entries are stored in-memory and respect the `revalidate` and `expire` times from your `cacheLife` configuration. You can customize the cache storage by configuring [`cacheHandlers`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) in your `next.config.js` file. 320 321 On the **client**, content from the server cache is stored in the browser's memory for the duration defined by the `stale` time. The client router enforces a **minimum 30-second stale time**, regardless of configuration. 322 323 The `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header communicates cache lifetime from server to client, ensuring coordinated behavior. 324 325 ## Revalidation 326 327 Cached functions revalidate based on the `revalidate` and `expire` times in their `cacheLife` profile, or on-demand through tags. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and are often paired: 328 329 - **[Time-based](#time-based-revalidation)**: refresh automatically after a set duration with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 330 - **[On-demand](#on-demand-revalidation)**: invalidate after a mutation with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) and [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag). 331 332 For example, a blog post that changes only when its author edits it can use a long `cacheLife` like `max` with a `cacheTag`, then invalidate on demand when the post is saved. A list of recent posts that updates throughout the day can use a shorter profile like `hours` to refresh on its own, without manual invalidation. 333 334 ### Time-based revalidation 335 336 Set an explicit cache lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) in every `use cache` scope. It makes the cache behavior clear at the call site, instead of depending on the `default` profile or surrounding caches. 337 338 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 339 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 340 341 async function getData() { 342 'use cache' 343 cacheLife('hours') // Use built-in 'hours' profile 344 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 345 return res.json() 346 } 347 ``` 348 349 If you omit `cacheLife`, the `default` profile applies and the lifetime is no longer explicit at the call site: 350 351 - **stale**: 5 minutes (client-side) 352 - **revalidate**: 15 minutes (server-side) 353 - **expire**: never expires by time 354 355 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 356 async function getData() { 357 'use cache' 358 // Implicitly uses the 'default' profile 359 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 360 return res.json() 361 } 362 ``` 363 364 Nesting a short-lived use cache inside one without an explicit [cacheLife](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) fails the build during prerendering. See [Nested short-lived caches](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-short-lived-caches) for the rule and fix. 365 366 ### On-demand revalidation 367 368 Use [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag), [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) for on-demand cache invalidation: 369 370 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 371 import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 372 373 async function getProducts() { 374 'use cache' 375 cacheTag('products') 376 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products') 377 return res.json() 378 } 379 ``` 380 381 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" 382 'use server' 383 384 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 385 386 export async function updateProduct() { 387 await db.products.update(...) 388 updateTag('products') // Invalidates all 'products' caches 389 } 390 ``` 391 392 Both `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` integrate across client and server caching layers, meaning you configure your caching semantics in one place and they apply everywhere. 393 394 ## Examples 395 396 ### Caching function output with `use cache` 397 398 You can add `use cache` to any asynchronous function, not only to components and routes. You might want to cache a network request, a database query, or a slow computation. 399 400 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={2} switcher 401 export async function getData() { 402 'use cache' 403 404 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 405 const data = await res.json() 406 return data 407 } 408 ``` 409 410 ```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={2} switcher 411 export async function getData() { 412 'use cache' 413 414 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 415 const data = await res.json() 416 return data 417 } 418 ``` 419 420 ### Caching a component's output with `use cache` 421 422 You can use `use cache` at the component level to cache any fetches or computations performed within that component. The cache entry will be reused as long as the serialized props produce the same value in each instance. 423 424 ```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" highlight={2} switcher 425 export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) { 426 'use cache' 427 async function getBookingsData() { 428 const response = await fetch( 429 `https://api.example.com/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}` 430 ) 431 const data = await response.json() 432 return data 433 } 434 return //... 435 } 436 437 interface BookingsProps { 438 type: string 439 } 440 ``` 441 442 ```jsx filename="app/components/bookings.js" highlight={2} switcher 443 export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }) { 444 'use cache' 445 async function getBookingsData() { 446 const response = await fetch( 447 `https://api.example.com/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}` 448 ) 449 const data = await response.json() 450 return data 451 } 452 return //... 453 } 454 ``` 455 456 ### Interleaving 457 458 In React, composition with `children` or slots is a well-known pattern for building flexible components. When using `use cache`, you can continue to compose your UI in this way. Anything included as `children`, or other compositional slots, in the returned JSX will be passed through the cached component without affecting its cache entry. 459 460 As long as you don't directly reference any of the JSX slots inside the body of the cacheable function itself, their presence in the returned output won't affect the cache entry. 461 462 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 463 export default async function Page() { 464 const uncachedData = await getData() 465 return ( 466 // Pass compositional slots as props, e.g. header and children 467 Home}> 468 {/* DynamicComponent is provided as the children slot */} 469 470 471 ) 472 } 473 474 async function CacheComponent({ 475 header, // header: a compositional slot, injected as a prop 476 children, // children: another slot for nested composition 477 }: { 478 header: ReactNode 479 children: ReactNode 480 }) { 481 'use cache' 482 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/cached-data') 483 const cachedData = await res.json() 484 return ( 485

515 {header} 516 517 {children} 518
519 ) 520 } 521 ``` 522 523 You can also pass Server Actions through cached components to Client Components without invoking them inside the cacheable function. 524 525 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 526 import ClientComponent from './ClientComponent' 527 528 export default async function Page() { 529 const performUpdate = async () => { 530 'use server' 531 // Perform some server-side update 532 await db.update(...) 533 } 534 535 return 536 } 537 538 async function CachedComponent({ 539 performUpdate, 540 }: { 541 performUpdate: () => Promise 542 }) { 543 'use cache' 544 // Do not call performUpdate here 545 return 546 } 547 ``` 548 549 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 550 import ClientComponent from './ClientComponent' 551 552 export default async function Page() { 553 const performUpdate = async () => { 554 'use server' 555 // Perform some server-side update 556 await db.update(...) 557 } 558 559 return 560 } 561 562 async function CachedComponent({ performUpdate }) { 563 'use cache' 564 // Do not call performUpdate here 565 return 566 } 567 ``` 568 569 ```tsx filename="app/ClientComponent.tsx" switcher 570 'use client' 571 572 export default function ClientComponent({ 573 action, 574 }: { 575 action: () => Promise 576 }) { 577 return 578 } 579 ``` 580 581 ```jsx filename="app/ClientComponent.js" switcher 582 'use client' 583 584 export default function ClientComponent({ action }) { 585 return 586 } 587 ``` 588 589 ### Caching a module's exports with `use cache` 590 591 Placing the directive at the top of a file covers every export, instead of repeating it on each one. Every exported function it covers must be async. 592 593 ```tsx filename="app/lib/reports.ts" 594 'use cache' 595 596 export async function getMonthlyTotals(accountId: string) { 597 return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } }) 598 } 599 600 export async function getTopProducts() { 601 return db.products.findMany({ orderBy: { sales: 'desc' }, take: 10 }) 602 } 603 ``` 604 605 Framework function exports are covered like any other, so [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) and [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) must be async in such a file. 606 607 > **Good to know**: 608 > 609 > - When a cached directive (`use cache`, [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), or [`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote)) is at the top of a file, you can import its exported functions into a Client Component and call them directly; they run on the server and return the result, similar to a [Server Function](/docs/app/glossary#server-function). With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 21 22 ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 23 24 The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 25 26 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 27 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 28 29 Install the skill: 30 31 ```bash filename="Terminal" 32 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 33 ``` 34 35 Then give the agent this prompt: 36 37 ```prompt 38 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 39 ``` 40 41 ## Or migrate by hand 42 43 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 44 45 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 46 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 47 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API. 48 49 Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working as a separate layer, so let the insights and errors guide what to change. 50 51 Some surfaces have their own steps: 52 53 - For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 54 - For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance. 55 56 The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components. 57 58 ## Enable Cache Components 59 60 Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. 61 62 Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: 63 64 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 65 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 66 67 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 68 cacheComponents: true, 69 } 70 71 export default nextConfig 72 ``` 73 74 > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 75 76 After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. 77 78 ## Opting out of validation 79 80 A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. Resolve it by following the recommendation: cache the data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrap it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're not ready to address it yet, set the [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) config to `false` on the segment that raised it (a layout, page, or parallel slot), then come back to it later. 81 82 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 83 export const instant = false 84 ``` 85 86 > **Good to know**: `instant = false` marks a segment as _allowed to block_. It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 87 88 ## Adopting incrementally 89 90 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 91 92 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. Routes that still render instantly need no further work. 93 2. **Opt out the routes that aren't ready.** Where an insight or error appears, set `instant = false` on the segment that raised it. To do this in one pass across the whole app, run the [`cache-components-instant-false`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#cache-components-instant-false) codemod, which adds the opt-out to every `page`, `layout`, and `default` that doesn't already declare `instant`: 94 95 ```bash filename="Terminal" 96 npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app 97 ``` 98 99 > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count. 100 101 The app keeps building and serving, now with validation deferred for the opted-out routes. 102 103 3. **Fix synchronous IO. It can't be deferred.** Calls like `new Date()`, `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` during prerender throw a build error that `instant = false` does not clear, so a route that uses them won't build until you address it, opt-out or not. Move the call out of the prerendered shell so it runs at request time: wrap the part that needs it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) and call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the call, or move it into a Client Component. 104 4. **Convert one route at a time.** Remove `instant = false` from a route, then resolve its insights by caching data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). Repeat until no routes opt out. 105 106 ## Following validation 107 108 Cache Components validates your routes in development and surfaces errors and insights in the dev overlay. Some look like this, naming the affected component and pointing at a fix: 109 110 111 ' }, 119 { text: '}' }, 120 ]} 121 /> 122 ', highlight: true }, 128 { text: ' ' }, 129 { text: '', highlight: true }, 130 ]} 131 /> 132 133 134 Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs. Work through the insights and errors until they're gone. For the full validation workflow, the DevTools, and CI testing, see the [instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation). 135 136 Insights don't show up in the HTTP response. An offending route still returns `200` with rendered HTML in dev. The insight only appears in the dev overlay, the dev-server log, or the [MCP `get_errors` tool](/docs/app/guides/mcp). To see them, read the overlay (or query the MCP). 137 138 ## `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` 139 140 **Not needed.** All pages are dynamic by default. 141 142 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 143 // Before - No longer needed 144 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 145 146 export default function Page() { 147 return
...
148 } 149 ``` 150 151 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 152 // Before - No longer needed 153 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 154 155 export default function Page() { 156 return
...
157 } 158 ``` 159 160 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 161 // After - Just remove it 162 export default function Page() { 163 return
...
164 } 165 ``` 166 167 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 168 // After - Just remove it 169 export default function Page() { 170 return
...
171 } 172 ``` 173 174 ## `dynamic = "force-static"` 175 176 Start by removing it. When unhandled uncached or runtime data access is detected during development and build time, Next.js raises an error. Otherwise, the prerendering step automatically extracts the static HTML shell. 177 178 For uncached data access, add [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) as close to the data access as possible with a long [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) like `'max'` to maintain cached behavior. If needed, add it at the top of the page or layout. 179 180 For runtime data access (`cookies()`, `headers()`, etc.), errors will direct you to wrap it with ``. Since you started by using `force-static`, you must remove the runtime data access to prevent any request time work. 181 182 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 183 // Before 184 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 185 186 export default async function Page() { 187 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 188 return
...
189 } 190 ``` 191 192 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 193 // Before 194 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 195 196 export default async function Page() { 197 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 198 return
...
199 } 200 ``` 201 202 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 203 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 204 205 // After - Use 'use cache' instead 206 export default async function Page() { 207 'use cache' 208 cacheLife('max') 209 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 210 return
...
211 } 212 ``` 213 214 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 215 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 216 217 // After - Use 'use cache' instead 218 export default async function Page() { 219 'use cache' 220 cacheLife('max') 221 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 222 return
...
223 } 224 ``` 225 226 ## `revalidate` 227 228 **Replace with `cacheLife`.** Use the `cacheLife` function to define cache duration instead of the route segment config. 229 230 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 231 // Before 232 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 233 234 export default async function Page() { 235 return
...
236 } 237 ``` 238 239 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 240 // Before 241 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 242 243 export default async function Page() { 244 return
...
245 } 246 ``` 247 248 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 249 // After - Use cacheLife 250 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 251 252 export default async function Page() { 253 'use cache' 254 cacheLife('hours') 255 return
...
256 } 257 ``` 258 259 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 260 // After - Use cacheLife 261 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 262 263 export default async function Page() { 264 'use cache' 265 cacheLife('hours') 266 return
...
267 } 268 ``` 269 270 > **Good to know**: If your `revalidate` value doesn't match a built-in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) profile (`'seconds'`, `'minutes'`, `'hours'`, `'days'`, `'weeks'`, `'max'`), pick the closest one or define a [custom profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#custom-cache-profiles) to match your conventions. You can also [redefine a built-in profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#overriding-the-default-cache-profiles), including `default`, when its timings don't match your application's caching needs. 271 272 ## `fetchCache` 273 274 **Not needed.** With `use cache`, all data fetching within a cached scope is automatically cached, making `fetchCache` unnecessary. 275 276 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 277 // Before 278 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 279 ``` 280 281 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 282 // Before 283 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 284 ``` 285 286 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 287 // After - Use 'use cache' to control caching behavior 288 export default async function Page() { 289 'use cache' 290 // All fetches here are cached 291 return
...
292 } 293 ``` 294 295 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 296 // After - Use 'use cache' to control caching behavior 297 export default async function Page() { 298 'use cache' 299 // All fetches here are cached 300 return
...
301 } 302 ``` 303 304 ## `fetch` cache options 305 306 **Move `cache` and `next` options to `use cache`.** 307 308 Without Cache Components, you cache a request with `cache: 'force-cache'` and tune it with `next: { revalidate, tags }`. 309 310 With Cache Components, wrap the fetch in a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) function. Fetches inside that scope are cached automatically, and `revalidate` and `tags` become [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 311 312 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 313 // Before 314 export default async function Page() { 315 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 316 cache: 'force-cache', 317 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 318 }) 319 const data = await res.json() 320 return
...
321 } 322 ``` 323 324 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 325 // Before 326 export default async function Page() { 327 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 328 cache: 'force-cache', 329 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 330 }) 331 const data = await res.json() 332 return
...
333 } 334 ``` 335 336 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 337 // After 338 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 339 340 async function getData() { 341 'use cache' 342 cacheLife('hours') 343 cacheTag('data') 344 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 345 return res.json() 346 } 347 348 export default async function Page() { 349 const data = await getData() 350 return
...
351 } 352 ``` 353 354 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 355 // After 356 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 357 358 async function getData() { 359 'use cache' 360 cacheLife('hours') 361 cacheTag('data') 362 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 363 return res.json() 364 } 365 366 export default async function Page() { 367 const data = await getData() 368 return
...
369 } 370 ``` 371 372 Note the persistence difference. The `fetch` Data Cache persists cached responses across deployments and across serverless instances. 373 374 `use cache` defaults to in-memory storage, so its entries are discarded when the serverless instance is destroyed and are scoped to a single deployment. Use [`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) or a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) for storage that survives instance teardown. Even with durable storage, expect cached values to recompute after a new deployment. 375 376 ## `unstable_cache` 377 378 **Replace with `use cache`.** 379 380 `unstable_cache` is replaced by the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. 381 382 Turn the wrapped function into a function with the `'use cache'` directive. The cache key is derived automatically from the arguments, so the key-parts array is no longer needed, and the `options` object maps to [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 383 384 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 385 // Before 386 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 387 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 388 389 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 390 async (id: string) => { 391 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 392 }, 393 ['user'], // cache key prefix 394 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 395 ) 396 ``` 397 398 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 399 // Before 400 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 401 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 402 403 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 404 async (id) => { 405 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 406 }, 407 ['user'], // cache key prefix 408 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 409 ) 410 ``` 411 412 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 413 // After 414 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 415 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 416 417 export async function getUser(id: string) { 418 'use cache' 419 cacheLife('hours') 420 cacheTag('users') 421 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 422 } 423 ``` 424 425 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 426 // After 427 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 428 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 429 430 export async function getUser(id) { 431 'use cache' 432 cacheLife('hours') 433 cacheTag('users') 434 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 435 } 436 ``` 437 438 Like the `fetch` Data Cache, `unstable_cache` persists cached values across deployments and serverless instances, while `use cache` does not. See [`fetch` cache options](#fetch-cache-options) above for the storage details. 439 440 ## `React.cache` 441 442 **Usually no change.** `React.cache` continues to deduplicate matching calls within a React render. 443 444 However, each Cache Function has an isolated React cache scope. Calls from separate Cache Functions do not share a `React.cache` result, such as when one Cache Function preloads data and another consumes it. 445 446 When a helper reads request data and matching calls need to share work across Cache Function scopes, replace the React wrapper with [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). If the function only needs request-scoped deduplication, use `cacheLife({ stale: Infinity })` so it does not lower the route's stale time. Private Cache Function results are not stored in a server cache across production requests. 447 448 ## On-demand revalidation (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`, `updateTag`) 449 450 On-demand invalidation still works by tagging cached data and expiring it after an event. Tag data with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside a `use cache` function instead of the `fetch` `next.tags` option, then choose the invalidation API by the behavior you want: 451 452 - [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag): for mutations whose result the user must see immediately (read-your-own-writes). Called from a Server Action, it expires the tag so the next request waits for fresh data instead of serving stale content. 453 - [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag): for stale-while-revalidate. A cache profile is **required** as the second argument, for example use `'max'` to serve cached data while it refreshes in the background. Works in Server Actions and Route Handlers. 454 - [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath): unchanged from the previous caching model. 455 456 `updateTag` isn't exclusive to Cache Components (it also works with the previous caching model), but migrating is a good time to adopt it. After a mutation in a Server Action, reach for it when the user should see their own change right away. 457 458 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 459 'use server' 460 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 461 462 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 463 // Create the post, then show it immediately on the next request 464 updateTag('posts') 465 } 466 ``` 467 468 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 469 'use server' 470 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 471 472 export async function createPost(formData) { 473 // Create the post, then show it immediately on the next request 474 updateTag('posts') 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 > **Good to know:** `updateTag` can only be called from a Server Action; calling it elsewhere throws. In Route Handlers or webhooks, use `revalidateTag` instead with a cache profile. 479 480 Pass `'max'` as the second argument to `revalidateTag` to expire the tag with stale-while-revalidate semantics: 481 482 ```tsx filename="app/api/webhook/route.ts" switcher 483 // Before 484 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 485 486 export async function POST() { 487 revalidateTag('posts') 488 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 489 } 490 ``` 491 492 ```js filename="app/api/webhook/route.js" switcher 493 // Before 494 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 495 496 export async function POST() { 497 revalidateTag('posts') 498 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 499 } 500 ``` 501 502 ```tsx filename="app/api/webhook/route.ts" switcher 503 // After - Pass a cache profile 504 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 505 506 export async function POST() { 507 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 508 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 ```js filename="app/api/webhook/route.js" switcher 513 // After - Pass a cache profile 514 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 515 516 export async function POST() { 517 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 518 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 519 } 520 ``` 521 522 ## `unstable_noStore` 523 524 **Not needed.** `unstable_noStore` (`noStore()`) opts a component out of caching. With Cache Components, nothing is cached unless you add `use cache`, so you can remove it. If a component must run at request time, call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the work and wrap it in ``. 525 526 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 527 // Before 528 import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache' 529 530 export default async function Page() { 531 noStore() 532 const data = await db.query('...') 533 return
...
534 } 535 ``` 536 537 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 538 // Before 539 import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache' 540 541 export default async function Page() { 542 noStore() 543 const data = await db.query('...') 544 return
...
545 } 546 ``` 547 548 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 549 // After - uncached by default, just remove noStore() 550 export default async function Page() { 551 const data = await db.query('...') 552 return
...
553 } 554 ``` 555 556 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 557 // After - uncached by default, just remove noStore() 558 export default async function Page() { 559 const data = await db.query('...') 560 return
...
561 } 562 ``` 563 564 ## `generateStaticParams` and `dynamicParams` 565 566 Cache Components changes how [dynamic routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) handle params. 567 568 ### `generateStaticParams` must return at least one param 569 570 **Returning an empty array now errors.** Without Cache Components, returning `[]` defers every path to the first runtime visit. With Cache Components, [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) must return at least one param so Next.js can prerender the route and validate it produces a non-empty [static shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell). An empty array raises [`empty-generate-static-params`](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). 571 572 Keep `generateStaticParams` and return at least one real param. Removing the export opts the route out of ISR, so Next.js renders it on every request, even when it uses `use cache` for data. Read [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) to learn how `generateStaticParams` prerenders dynamic routes and how unlisted paths behave. 573 574 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 575 // Before - defer all paths to runtime 576 export async function generateStaticParams() { 577 return [] 578 } 579 ``` 580 581 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 582 // Before - defer all paths to runtime 583 export async function generateStaticParams() { 584 return [] 585 } 586 ``` 587 588 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 589 // After - return at least one param to prerender 590 export async function generateStaticParams() { 591 const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json()) 592 return posts.slice(0, 1).map((post) => ({ slug: post.slug })) 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 597 // After - return at least one param to prerender 598 export async function generateStaticParams() { 599 const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json()) 600 return posts.slice(0, 1).map((post) => ({ slug: post.slug })) 601 } 602 ``` 603 604 Paths you don't return are still served at request time. 605 606 > **Good to know:** When you use `generateStaticParams` without Partial Prefetching, await `params` outside `` to preserve ISR for unlisted paths. To serve a fallback while an unlisted path renders, enable [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) and await `params` inside ``. See [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for details. 607 608 ### `dynamicParams` is not supported 609 610 **Delete the export.** With Cache Components enabled, exporting `dynamicParams` fails the build with this error message: 611 612 > Route segment config "dynamicParams" is not compatible with `nextConfig.cacheComponents`. 613 614 Params not returned by `generateStaticParams` are rendered on request. If you used `dynamicParams: false` to reject them, call [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) in the page when the param doesn't resolve to real data. 615 616 ### Await `params` inside `` 617 618 For routes that don't use `generateStaticParams`, pass the `params` promise into a [``](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) boundary instead of awaiting it at the top of the component. This lets Next.js prerender a static shell while the params remain unknown. For routes that use `generateStaticParams`, follow the ISR guidance above. 619 620 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 621 // Before - awaiting params at the top blocks the shell 622 export default async function Page({ 623 params, 624 }: { 625 params: Promise<{ slug: string }> 626 }) { 627 const { slug } = await params 628 return 629 } 630 ``` 631 632 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 633 // Before - awaiting params at the top blocks the shell 634 export default async function Page({ params }) { 635 const { slug } = await params 636 return 637 } 638 ``` 639 640 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 641 import { Suspense } from 'react' 642 643 // After - await inside Suspense so the shell can prerender 644 export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 645 return ( 646 Loading...}> 647 648 649 ) 650 } 651 652 async function Post({ params }: Pick, 'params'>) { 653 const { slug } = await params 654 // ... 655 } 656 ``` 657 658 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 659 import { Suspense } from 'react' 660 661 // After - await inside Suspense so the shell can prerender 662 export default function Page({ params }) { 663 return ( 664 Loading...}> 665 666 667 ) 668 } 669 670 async function Post({ params }) { 671 const { slug } = await params 672 // ... 673 } 674 ``` 675 676 Client hooks that read the route follow the same Suspense pattern. When the route's pathname is fully known, they resolve during prerendering and need no boundary. When the pathname depends on dynamic params not yet known, the hooks suspend wherever the component sits. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component. 15 16 ## Usage 17 18 ### Basic setup 19 20 To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file: 21 22 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 23 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 24 25 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 26 cacheComponents: true, 27 } 28 29 export default nextConfig 30 ``` 31 32 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 33 const nextConfig = { 34 cacheComponents: true, 35 } 36 37 module.exports = nextConfig 38 ``` 39 40 `cacheLife` can only be used within a cache directive scope. 41 42 Add a cache directive (for example, `use cache`) at the file level or at the top of an async function or component. 43 44 `cacheLife` cannot be used at module scope. Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error. 45 46 > **Good to know**: 47 > 48 > - We recommend setting a `cacheLife` in every `use cache` scope so its behavior is clear at the call site. Omitting it leaves the lifetime implicit (the `default` profile applies), which makes it harder to reason about, for example in [nested cached scopes](#nested-caching-behavior). 49 > - Call `cacheLife` in the same function or component where caching is defined. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about. 50 > - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example. 51 52 ### Using preset profiles 53 54 Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors: 55 56 - How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side) 57 - How often fresh content is generated on the server 58 - When old content expires completely 59 60 Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes: 61 62 - **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores) 63 - **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news) 64 - **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather) 65 - **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles) 66 - **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters) 67 - **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content) 68 69 Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name: 70 71 ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5} 72 'use cache' 73 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 74 75 export default async function BlogPage() { 76 cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily 77 78 const posts = await getBlogPosts() 79 return
{/* render posts */}
80 } 81 ``` 82 83 The profile name tells Next.js how to cache the entire function's output. If you don't call `cacheLife`, the `default` profile is used. See [preset cache profiles](#preset-cache-profiles) for timing details. 84 85 ## Reference 86 87 ### Cache profile properties 88 89 Cache profiles control caching behavior through three timing properties: 90 91 - **[`stale`](#stale)**: How long the client can use cached data without checking the server 92 - **[`revalidate`](#revalidate)**: After this time, the next request will trigger a background refresh 93 - **[`expire`](#expire)**: After this time with no requests, the next one waits for fresh content 94 95 #### `stale` 96 97 **Client-side:** How long the client can use cached data without checking the server. 98 99 During this time, the client-side router displays cached content immediately without any network request. After this period expires, the router must check with the server on the next navigation or request. This provides instant page loads from the client cache, but data may be outdated. 100 101 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `stale` value (5 minutes, see [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) 102 - Also determines whether the content can be part of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). See [Prerendering behavior](#prerendering-behavior). 103 104 ```tsx 105 cacheLife({ stale: 300 }) // 5 minutes 106 ``` 107 108 #### `revalidate` 109 110 How often the server regenerates cached content in the background. 111 112 - When a request arrives after this period, the server: 113 1. Serves the cached version immediately (if available) 114 2. Regenerates content in the background 115 3. Updates the cache with fresh content 116 - Similar to [Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration) 117 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `revalidate` value (15 minutes) 118 119 ```tsx 120 cacheLife({ revalidate: 900 }) // 15 minutes 121 ``` 122 123 #### `expire` 124 125 Maximum time before the server must regenerate cached content. 126 127 - After this period with no traffic, the server regenerates content synchronously on the next request 128 - When you set both `revalidate` and `expire`, `expire` must be longer than `revalidate`. Next.js validates this and raises an error for invalid configurations. 129 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `expire` value (never expires) 130 131 ```tsx 132 cacheLife({ expire: 3600 }) // 1 hour 133 ``` 134 135 ### Preset cache profiles 136 137 If you don't specify a profile, Next.js uses the `default` profile. We recommend explicitly setting a profile to make caching behavior clear. 138 139 | **Profile** | **Use Case** | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` | 140 | ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | -------- | 141 | `default` | Standard content | 5 minutes | 15 minutes | never | 142 | `seconds` | Real-time data | 30 seconds | 1 second | 1 minute | 143 | `minutes` | Frequently updated content | 5 minutes | 1 minute | 1 hour | 144 | `hours` | Content updated multiple times per day | 5 minutes | 1 hour | 1 day | 145 | `days` | Content updated daily | 5 minutes | 1 day | 1 week | 146 | `weeks` | Content updated weekly | 5 minutes | 1 week | 30 days | 147 | `max` | Stable content that rarely changes | 5 minutes | 30 days | 1 year | 148 149 ### Overriding the default cache profiles 150 151 The preset profiles map to familiar time periods (`seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `weeks`), alongside `default` and `max`. You can use these as they are, or redefine any of them, including `default` and `max`, in `next.config.ts`. The built-in names keep working with editor autocomplete. 152 153 Redefining a built-in is a supported pattern, but document it in your project so a call like `cacheLife('hours')` reflects the values you set, not the presets. The time-named profiles carry an intuitive expectation (`days` reads as roughly 24 hours), so redefining them is more likely to surprise a reader than redefining `default` or `max`, which don't imply a specific duration. An equally valid approach is to define your own [custom profile](#custom-cache-profiles) rather than overloading a built-in name. 154 155 Redefining `default` also changes the lifetime applied when a `use cache` scope calls no `cacheLife`. The example below sets `default` to a one hour revalidate: 156 157 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 158 const nextConfig = { 159 cacheComponents: true, 160 cacheLife: { 161 // Redefine the 'default' profile 162 default: { 163 stale: 300, // 5 minutes 164 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 165 expire: 86400, // 1 day 166 }, 167 }, 168 } 169 170 export default nextConfig 171 ``` 172 173 > **Good to know:** The `cacheLife` function's type signature is generated from `next.config.ts` during `next dev`, `next build`, or [`next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options), so an overridden profile's editor autocomplete and JSDoc hint reflect the values you set, not the presets. 174 175 ### Custom cache profiles 176 177 Define reusable cache profiles with your own names in `next.config.ts`: 178 179 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 180 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 181 182 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 183 cacheComponents: true, 184 cacheLife: { 185 biweekly: { 186 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 187 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 188 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 189 }, 190 }, 191 } 192 193 export default nextConfig 194 ``` 195 196 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 197 const nextConfig = { 198 cacheComponents: true, 199 cacheLife: { 200 biweekly: { 201 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 202 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 203 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 204 }, 205 }, 206 } 207 208 module.exports = nextConfig 209 ``` 210 211 The example above caches for 14 days, checks for updates daily, and expires the cache after 14 days. Page
222 } 223 ``` 224 225 ### Inline cache profiles 226 227 For one-off cases, pass a profile object directly to `cacheLife`: 228 229 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 230 'use cache' 231 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 232 233 export default async function Page() { 234 cacheLife({ 235 stale: 3600, 236 revalidate: 900, 237 expire: 86400, 238 }) 239 240 return
Page
241 } 242 ``` 243 244 Inline profiles apply only to the specific function or component. For reusable configurations, define custom profiles in `next.config.ts`. 245 246 Using `cacheLife({})` with an empty object applies the `default` profile values. 247 248 ### Client cache behavior 249 250 The `stale` property controls the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache), not the `Cache-Control` header: 251 252 - The server sends the stale time via the `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header 253 - The client router uses this value to determine when to revalidate 254 - **Minimum of 30 seconds is enforced** to ensure prefetched links remain usable 255 256 This 30-second minimum prevents prefetched data from expiring before users can click on links. 14	
15	The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
16	
17	## Usage
18	
19	To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
20	
21	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
22	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
23	
24	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
25	  cacheComponents: true,
26	}
27	
28	export default nextConfig
29	```
30	
31	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
32	const nextConfig = {
33	  cacheComponents: true,
34	}
35	
36	module.exports = nextConfig
37	```
38	
39	The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
40	
41	```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
42	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
43	
44	export async function getData() {
45	  'use cache'
46	  cacheTag('my-data')
47	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
48	  const data = await res.json()
49	  return data
50	}
51	```
52	
53	```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
54	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
55	
56	export async function getData() {
57	  'use cache'
58	  cacheTag('my-data')
59	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
60	  const data = await res.json()
61	  return data
62	}
63	```
64	
65	You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
66	
67	- Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
68	- Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
69	
70	For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
71	
72	```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
73	'use server'
74	
75	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
76	
77	export default async function submit() {
78	  await addPost()
79	  updateTag('my-data')
80	}
81	```
82	
83	```jsx filename="app/action.js" switcher
84	'use server'
85	
86	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
87	
88	export default async function submit() {
89	  await addPost()
90	  updateTag('my-data')
91	}
92	```
93	
94	## Good to know
95	
96	- **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.
97	- **Multiple Tags**: You can assign multiple tags to a single cache entry by passing multiple string values to `cacheTag`.
98	
99	```tsx
100	cacheTag('tag-one', 'tag-two')
101	```
102	
103	- **Limits**: A single `cacheTag()` call accepts up to 128 tags, each with a maximum length of 256 characters. Tags longer than 256 characters are skipped, and any tags past the 128th in one call are dropped. Both cases log a console warning.
104	
105	## Examples
106	
107	### Tagging components or functions
108	
109	Tag your cached data by calling `cacheTag` within a cached function or component:
110	
111	```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
112	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
113	
114	interface BookingsProps {
115	  type: string
116	}
117	
118	export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
119	  'use cache'
120	  cacheTag('bookings-data')
121	
122	  async function getBookingsData() {
123	    const response = await fetch(
124	      `https://api.example.com/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`
125	    )
126	    const data = await response.json()
127	    return data
128	  }
129	
130	  return //...
131	}
132	```
133

15	The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.

17	## Usage

19	To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
